land.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

predecessors.note: Alans page: In 442 Aetius had Goar settle many followers in the Orléanais, to police the bacaudae of Armorica and block the Visigoths at the Loire. The Alans of Valence (440) are a separate settlement with no later page. Western-roman-empire holds all 84 cells of the Orléanais until its 476 loss, which hands northern Gaul to kingdom-of-soissons (73 of the 84 cells).

land.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

successors.note: Soissons page: after the battle of 486 Clovis 'took over all his territory' and 'the domain was thereafter under the control of the Franks'; salian-franks_486 holds the Domain of Soissons with its 'border on the Loire'. The Alans page: 'Around 502-503 Clovis attacked Armorica but was defeated by the Alans', then 'an accord was arranged by which Clovis came to rule the various peoples of Armorica'. The pages do not say Orléans passed to Clovis in 503; the land lies inside the Salian shape from 486 and the Alan state is closed in 503 as a bridge. The Sangiban page has a different end: 'the Alans of Aurelianum were conquered by the Visigoths a few years later' than 451, 'incorporated into the Gothic Kingdom of Toulouse'; the Alans page has them beat the Goths at Orléans in 463, and the Soissons page has the same battle won on Soissons's side.

capitals.name: Aurelianum (Orléans)
capitals.note: The Sangiban page gives 'the region around Aurelianum' as the Alan foederati's seat, not a capital; Orléans is the central place of the Orléanais, a reading.

correction.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 442-503: the Alan federates on the middle Loire. In 442 Aetius had Goar settle many followers in the Orléanais (Alans page); 'He settled the Alans around Valence in 440 and along the Loire including Aurelianum in 442 to contain unrest in Armorica' (Aetius page); Sangiban was 'king of the Alan foederati settled in the region around Aurelianum'. No area or boundary is given: the Orléanais region (about 8,000-10,000 km2) is the page's own name. Armorica, where the Alans put down the Bagaudae in 447/448 and fought Clovis in 502/503, is a field of operation, not drawn as their land. Infobox area: none on the page. Overlaps (gazetteer, 2026-10-24, review of eu-06-x): the 84 cells (about 21,200 km2) lie 442-475 inside western-roman-empire (all 84 cells in 410-472, 73 in the 469 shape), 73 of them inside kingdom-of-soissons_476/480 (476-486) and salian-franks_486 to _507 (486-509), and 11 inside visigothic-kingdom_469 to _490 (the southern cells at the Loire). The first draft drew the Orléanais as the Alans' sole land for 476-503, which was Soissons's and then Clovis's land in the neighbouring dossiers. Resolution: from 476 the Alans are drawn as a federate/vassal tint over the land of kingdom-of-soissons (476-486) and then salian-franks (486-503), as under Rome before, with the sovereign's dossier holding the land. The Soissons page (read 2026-10-24) lists 'Alans and Britons and Saxons as well as other Roman administrators' among the domain's peoples, 'won the a battle at Orleans against the Visigoths in 463' and names a Count Paul against Visigothic attacks 'in the Loire region'; the Alans page is silent on who ruled Orléans after 476, so this tie is a confidence-1 reading. The 11 Visigothic cells are not removed (the Sangiban page has the Visigoths conquer the Alans of Aurelianum).

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 442: Aetius settles Goar's Alans round Orléans. 'In 442, after it became clear to Aetius that he could no longer rely upon the Huns for support', he had Goar settle many followers in the Orléanais, to police the bacaudae of Armorica and block the Visigoths at the Loire (Alans page); the Aetius page: 'along the Loire including Aurelianum in 442'. The Alans of Valence (440) are a second settlement the pages do not follow.

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 442: the Alans are Roman federates on the Loire. Sangiban was 'the successor of Goar as king of the Alan foederati settled in the region around Aurelianum' (Sangiban page); the year is the Alans page's. The pages do not call them vassals; the dossier follows the burgundian-kingdom model (federates in the lighter tint, empire as counterpart).

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 476: the Roman federation lapses with the Western Empire. The pages are silent on when the Alans ceased to be federates of Rome; 476 is the year of the last Western emperor's deposition ('deposed Romulus Augustulus on 4 September 476', Odoacer page; a bridge), and the western-roman-empire dossier's 476 loss hands northern Gaul to kingdom-of-soissons. In 463 and 466 the Alans act alone ('In 463 the Alans defeated the Goths at the battle of Orléans'; 'they later defeated the Franks led by Childeric in 466').

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 476: the Orléanais falls to Syagrius's Domain of Soissons and the Alans stay as its federates. The Soissons page: 'There were also Alans and Britons and Saxons as well as other Roman administrators using various titles'; the domain 'won the a battle at Orleans against the Visigoths in 463', and Count Paul led 'Roman and Frankish forces in the Loire region against Visigothic attacks'. The Alans page does not say who ruled Orléans after 476, so the tie is a bridge (confidence 1) that removes the double drawing of the Orléanais (73 of 84 cells in kingdom-of-soissons_476/480); the page disagrees on its extent ('a state controlling most of northern Gaul' against 'little more than a Count of Soissons').

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 486: Syagrius loses to Clovis. 'In 486, Syagrius lost the Battle of Soissons to the Frankish king Clovis I'; Clovis 'took over all his territory' and 'the domain was thereafter under the control of the Franks'. The Alans are not mentioned in the event; the end of their tie with Soissons is the end of the domain.

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: 486: the Alans of Orléans lie in Clovis's enlarged realm. salian-franks_486 holds the Domain of Soissons with its 'border on the Loire' (73 of the 84 cells of the Orléanais). Neither page says the Alans submitted; the Alans page has them beat Clovis's attack on Armorica in 502-503, which does not read as a vassal, so the relation is a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: About 503: the Alan tie ends with the accord. 'Around 502-503 Clovis attacked Armorica but was defeated by the Alans', then 'an accord was arranged by which Clovis came to rule the various peoples of Armorica'; the Alans are integrated into the Merovingian military structure. The page gives no date for the accord and the item concerns Armorica, not Orléans (confidence 1).

region.text: 'the Orléanais' / 'along the Loire including Aurelianum': the Alan foederati settled round Orléans

ledger.note: About 503: the Alan state ends. The last dated Alan item on the Alans page is Clovis's failed attack of 502-503 and the accord that integrated the Alans into Clovis's Merovingian military structure; the Sangiban page, in contrast, has them conquered by the Visigoths 'a few years' after 451 and 'incorporated into the Gothic Kingdom of Toulouse'. The end year is a bridge, not a statement of either page. No land changes hands in 503 (the Orléanais has been inside the Salian shape since 486), so there is no loss event; the Salian dossier (358-509) is the successor of record.

wars.name: Bagaudae revolt of Armorica
wars.outcome: 'The Bagaudae in Armorica revolted again in 447 or 448, and were put down by the Alans of Goar' (Aetius page).
wars.note: No ground changes hands; Armorica (Brittany) is the field of operations.

wars.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
wars.outcome: Sangiban's Alans, at Orléans, 'bore the main brunt of the Hunnic assault, while the Goths were able to flank the Huns' (Sangiban page, which gives 451 for Attila's invasion of Gaul).
wars.note: The Aetius page has Aetius persuade 'Sambida' (the Sangiban of the other page) to join him, 'falsely accused of planning to join the Huns'. No border change.

wars.name: Battle of Orléans (463)
wars.outcome: 'In 463 the Alans defeated the Goths at the battle of Orléans' (Alans page); the Loire frontier holds.
wars.note: The Sangiban page's statement that the Visigoths conquered the Alans of Aurelianum 'a few years' after 451 is not reconciled.

wars.name: Alan war with Childeric's Franks
wars.outcome: 'they later defeated the Franks led by Childeric in 466' (Alans page).
wars.note: No place is given. Childeric's Franks are the salian-franks dossier (358-509), not kingdom-of-the-franks.

wars.name: Clovis's attack on Armorica
wars.outcome: 'Around 502-503 Clovis attacked Armorica but was defeated by the Alans'; an accord follows and Clovis rules the peoples of Armorica; the Alans are absorbed into his army.
wars.note: The page puts the fight in Armorica, which the Alans do not hold in this dossier, so no zone is drawn (the salian-franks dossier adds Armorica in 501). The former zone, the Orléanais, was the land the first draft handed to the Franks at 503; the Orléanais is now Salian from 486 and the Alans its federates.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Orléanais is the page's own region name. From 476 the Alans are a federate tint over Soissons's and then Clovis's land, a reading.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-b (suggested slug alans-of-orleans, about 442-470s; the alans dossier covers only the Iberian Alans 409-418). Three pages opened; the dossier's length (442-503) rests on the Alans page's last dated item, while the Sangiban page makes it a few years after 451 and the 463 and 466 items continue it: end year confidence 1. The Alans of Valence (settled 440, Aetius page) have no further mention and are not drawn; Beorgor's Alans crossed the Alps in winter 464 and were beaten in Liguria by Ricimer (Alans page) and are not this state. Aetius's page has 'Sambida' where the Sangiban page has Sangiban. No area, no capital, no ruler list. Wikidata id unknown. The western-roman-empire dossier has no event for the 442 settlement; the kingdom-of-the-franks dossier (eu-07) has no 503 gain. Repair of 2026-10-24 (review eu-06-x): the Orléanais was drawn as the Alans' sole land 476-503 although 73 of 84 cells lie in kingdom-of-soissons_476/480 and salian-franks_486 to _507. It is now a federate/vassal tint over Soissons (476-486) and the Salian Franks (486-503), two vassal pairs (confidence 1 for the ties, 2 for the 486 end of the Soissons tie); the 503 loss is removed because no land changes hands, and kingdom-of-the-franks is replaced by salian-franks everywhere (successor, 503 dissolve, wars 466 and 502-503). Disagreement with the reviewer: none on the facts; the alternative of ending the dossier in 476 was not taken because the Alans page has the Alans acting in 463, 466 and 502-503. The 502-503 war zone is dropped (the page says Armorica). Direction of the federate events: see thracian-goths notes (the schema reads vassal_start's counterpart as the vassal). Requests: kingdom-of-soissons (eu-04) and salian-franks (eu-07) should hold a matching vassal_start/vassal_end for alans-of-orleans (476-486, 486-503; confidence 1); western-roman-empire (eu-04-b) the 442 vassal_start and 476 vassal_end. Pages tried: Goar (no later Alan rulers) and Goar_(Alan_king) (url_not_found).
